items.opening_verbatim: II Calendar No. 690 119th CONGRESS 2d Session S. 2378 [Report No. 119–157] IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES July 22, 2025 Mr. Moran (for himself, Mr. Van Hollen , Mr. Bennet , Mr. Boozman , Mr. Daines , Mr. Sheehy , Mrs. Capito , Mr. Hick
items.summary: S. 2378, the SAFEGUARDS Act of 2025 as reported by the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, amends 49 U.S.C. 44923 to revise the Aviation Security Capital Fund and establish an Aviation Security Checkpoint Technology Fund. For fiscal years 2026 through 2036, it directs the TSA Administrator to collect at least $400,000,000 annually for the capital fund and at least $250,000,000 annually for the checkpoint technology fund from fees under 49 U.S.C. 44940(a)(1). The bill also requires briefings and reports to Congress, biennial Inspector General audits through fiscal year 2036, and includes a sense of Congress on the use of the 9/11 Security Fee.
items.title: 119 S2378 RS: Spending Aviation Fees for Equipment, Guaranteeing Upgraded and Advanced Risk Detection and Safety Act of 2025

items.opening_verbatim: II Calendar No. 693 119th CONGRESS 2d Session S. 3226 IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES November 19, 2025 Mr. Crapo (for himself, Mrs. Shaheen , Mr. Risch , Mr. Padilla , Ms. Klobuchar , Ms. Duckworth , Ms. Rosen , Ms. Hassan , Ms. Hirono
items.summary: S. 3226, the Bring Our Heroes Home Act, as reported by the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, directs the Archivist of the United States to create a Missing Armed Forces and Civilian Personnel Records Collection at the National Archives. It requires Government offices to identify, copy, and transmit to the Archivist records relating to missing Armed Forces and civilian personnel from December 7, 1941 onward, prohibits their destruction or alteration, and requires certifications under penalty of perjury. The bill also establishes a Missing Armed Forces and Civilian Personnel Records Review Board and sets requirements for reports justifying any substantial redaction or withholding of records; the source text is truncated, and this summary covers only the sections shown.
items.title: 119 S3226 RS: Bring Our Heroes Home Act

items.summary: S. 4448, the Accelerating Broadband Permits Act of 2026, as reported by the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, directs the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information to publish a public dashboard tracking Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment (BEAD) grant recipients' expenditures and broadband service locations. It requires the Assistant Secretary to publish semiannual reports on BEAD grant progress, create a permit-tracking tool for eligible entities and subgrantees, develop data controls for communications use application processing times within 120 days, and establish an alert method for applications at risk of missing the 270-day deadline. The bill also amends the FAST Act definition of minimum broadband project cost to include NEPA-subject broadband infrastructure projects likely to require more than $5,000,000 in total investment.
items.title: 119 S4448 RS: Accelerating Broadband Permits Act of 2026

items.opening_verbatim: II Calendar No. 692 119th CONGRESS 2d Session S. 4691 [Report No. 119–159] IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES June 4, 2026 Mr. Sheehy (for himself and Ms. Klobuchar ) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the C
items.summary: S. 4691, the Disaster Communications Coordination and Preparedness Act, as reported without amendment by the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, directs the Federal Communications Commission to review its procedures for Disaster Information Reporting System (DIRS) activation and deactivation notices within 180 days. It requires the Commission to evaluate, within 18 months, the feasibility of enhancing its public safety liaison functions as a point of entry for State, local, Tribal, and territorial officials, and to develop plain-language awareness materials within one year. The bill states that it does not require the Commission to adopt new regulations or impose new reporting requirements on communications providers.
items.title: 119 S4691 RS: Disaster Communications Coordination and Preparedness Act

items.summary: On November 9, 2026, the Clerk of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit sent a letter to Brianda Genchi Garcia regarding Case No. 26-1501, Brianda Genchi Garcia v. Todd Blanche, stating that the court issued an opinion and entered judgment that day. The letter advises that petitions for rehearing and petitions for rehearing en banc must be received within 45 days of the entry of judgment, that counsel-filed petitions must be filed electronically in CM/ECF, and that no mailing grace period applies except under FRAP 25(a)(2)(iii). The letter states that a petition not received within the FRAP 40 period may be denied as untimely.

items.summary: The Tenth Circuit issued an unpublished order and judgment on November 9, 2026, in Bailey v. City of Ada, No. 25-7088, arising from a police shooting in which an officer shot Jeffrey Peterson after entering his apartment without a warrant. The court affirmed the district court's grant of summary judgment to the City of Ada on plaintiff's failure-to-train claim under 42 U.S.C. § 1983, concluding that plaintiff did not show the city's training was inadequate. The order states that it is not binding precedent except under the doctrines of law of the case, res judicata, and collateral estoppel.

items.summary: The Third Circuit issued a nonprecedential opinion on November 9, 2026, in Travelodge Hotels, Inc. v. Huber Hotels, LLC, No. 25-2808, on appeal from a bench-trial judgment of the District of New Jersey. The court held that the district court did not clearly err in finding that Travelodge materially breached a November 17, 2017 franchising agreement by failing to integrate a hotel in Hurley, Wisconsin into its reservation system within a reasonable time. The court affirmed the judgment in favor of Huber Hotels, LLC, Robert Huber, and Janette Huber.

items.summary: The Third Circuit issued a nonprecedential per curiam opinion on November 9, 2026, in McDowell v. Pennsylvania Department of Human Services, No. 26-1586, affirming the Middle District of Pennsylvania's dismissal with prejudice of pro se plaintiff Jennifer E. McDowell's amended complaint. The court found that the complaint's allegations of a statewide conspiracy by the Department of Human Services' Child Welfare Department were conclusory and did not state a plausible claim under Ashcroft v. Iqbal, and that further amendment would be futile. The court also denied McDowell's request to supplement the appellate record with extra-record allegations.

items.summary: The Third Circuit issued a nonprecedential per curiam opinion on November 9, 2026, in Gomez v. City of Pittsburgh, No. 26-1735, affirming the Western District of Pennsylvania's Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal of John Paul Gomez's amended complaint under 42 U.S.C. § 1983. The court held that Gomez identified no source for a duty to notify him of his ex-wife's 2019 arrest, and that his claims regarding the search and arrest of his adult son either could not be asserted by him or rested on conclusory allegations. The court did not reach the district court's alternative statute-of-limitations ruling.

items.summary: A memorandum dated November 10, 2026, from the President to the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture and the EPA Administrator determines that firefighting activities, including aerial use of fire retardants by the Forest Service, the Department of the Interior, other agencies, and their contractors, are exempt from Federal, State, interstate, and local water pollution control requirements under section 313 of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, except for requirements under 33 U.S.C. 1316 and 1317. The exemption covers the one-year period from November 10, 2026, to November 10, 2027, and the memorandum directs the Secretary of Agriculture to publish it in the Federal Register.
items.title: Presidential Determination Concerning Wildfire Suppression Activities in the United States

items.summary: In an unpublished per curiam opinion filed November 9, 2026, the Fifth Circuit affirmed the district court's denial of Deliris Montanez Berrios's second Rule 60(b) motion to reopen her suit against El Paso County Judge Ricardo Samaniego and Texas Secretary of State Robert S. Howden, and denied her motion for an injunction pending appeal. The court held that the motions to reopen were filed after the 28-day Rule 59 period and therefore did not toll the time to appeal, and that the appellate briefing did not identify a Rule 60(b) ground for relief. The panel also held that the injunction factors were not established, because the election records at issue were not shown to be at risk of loss.
items.title: Montanez Berrios v. Samaniego

items.summary: In an unpublished per curiam opinion filed November 9, 2026, the Fifth Circuit denied the petition for review filed by Joul Ghasan Ibrahim, a native and citizen of Syria, of a Board of Immigration Appeals decision affirming the denial of asylum, withholding of removal, and relief under the Convention Against Torture. The court held that the petitioner forfeited challenges to the BIA's determination that the petitioner had waived challenges under the Circumvention of Lawful Pathways rule, and that the petitioner did not show that no reasonable factfinder could make the adverse credibility determination. The court also found that the BIA had considered the country conditions evidence, and that general country conditions evidence did not establish an individualized risk of torture.

Hill of Arkansas addressed the House to recognize the Public Timber Project, a nonprofit supporting public hunting lands, which reported over 2,000 volunteer hours, 28 site cleanups, and more than 100 boat ramp cleanups. The statement also honors the late Lowell Baier, a conservationist and former Boone and Crockett Club president, and recognizes broadcaster Dave Woodman's 56 years of service in Arkansas media. items.summary: Rep. Massie gave notice of his intent to raise a question of the privileges of the House by offering a resolution to impeach Peter Brian Hegseth, Secretary of Defense. The draft articles of impeachment allege that Hegseth directed U.S. Armed Forces into hostilities against Iran beginning February 28, 2026, without a declaration of war, specific statutory authorization, or a national emergency as described in the War Powers Resolution of 1973. The articles further allege that hostilities continued after H. Con. Res. 86, a concurrent resolution directing removal of the forces, was agreed to by the House on June 3, 2026, and by the Senate on June 23, 2026.

NOMINATIONS

  Executive nominations received by the Senate:

                        FEDERAL TRADE COMMISSION

        CHRISTOPHER MUFARRIGE, OF TEXAS, TO BE A FEDERAL TRADE
     COMMISSIONER FOR THE TERM OF S
items.summary: The Senate received executive nominations including Christopher Mufarrige to be a Federal Trade Commissioner for a seven-year term, Michael Losapio to be Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, and Gary Lawkowski to be General Counsel of the Office of the Director of National Intelligence. Additional nominations include Arthur Kleinschmidt as Assistant Attorney General, federal district and circuit judges, Superior Court of the District of Columbia associate judges, ambassadors to Pakistan, the United Arab Emirates, Burundi, Senegal, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, and North Macedonia, and an Assistant Secretary of Energy. The nominations also include Army Reserve and Army National Guard promotions to brigadier general and colonel, and Army and Coast Guard appointments.

items.summary: This proposed rule would reform Medicare and Medicaid regulations deemed obsolete or excessively burdensome on healthcare providers and suppliers, with the objective of reducing costs, enhancing flexibility in delivering innovative care, and streamlining existing regulations. items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES Food and Drug Administration 21 CFR Part 73 [Docket No. FDA-2023-C-5679] Color Additive Petition From Environmental Defense Fund et al.; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the S
items.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is partially granting a color additive petition submitted by Environmental Defense Fund et al. (petitioners), by amending our color additive regulations, on the basis of the Delaney Clause, to remove the authorized use of methylene chloride as a diluent in color additive mixtures in inks for marking fruit and vegetables. The petitioners provided data demonstrating that this additive induces cancer in laboratory animals. We are denying the remaining petition requests to remove ethylene dichloride, methylene chloride, and trichloroethylene from the list of authorized extraction solvents for annatto extract, paprika oleoresin, and turmeric oleoresin, because any residue of the solvent would be an impurity in the color additive and such impurities are not subject to the Delaney Clause.
tags: department of health and human services
items.title: Color Additive Petition From Environmental Defense Fund et al.; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Ethylene Dichloride, Methylene Chloride, and Trichloroethylene

items.agency: DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES
items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES Food and Drug Administration 21 CFR Part 73 [Docket No. FDA-2026-C-3071] Color Additive Petition From the International Association of Color Manufacturers; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulati
items.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is partially granting a color additive petition submitted by the International Association of Color Manufacturers (IACM or petitioner), by amending our color additive regulations, on the basis of abandonment, to remove the authorized uses of methylene chloride, trichloroethylene, and ethylene dichloride from the list of authorized extraction solvents for annatto extract, paprika oleoresin, and turmeric oleoresin. The petitioner provided data demonstrating that these uses have been permanently abandoned. FDA is denying as moot the portion of the petition proposing that the color additive regulations be amended, on the basis of abandonment, to no longer authorize the use of methylene chloride as a diluent in color additive mixtures in inks for marking fruit and vegetables. This request is moot because the authorization for this use has been removed, on the basis of the Delaney Clause, in response to a separate petition.
tags: department of health and human services
items.title: Color Additive Petition From the International Association of Color Manufacturers; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Methylene Chloride, Trichloroethylene, and Ethylene Dichloride

items.summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is determining under the Clean Air Act (CAA) that the Detroit, Michigan Moderate nonattainment area (“Detroit area” or “area”) attained the 2015 ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) by the applicable attainment date. This determination relies on the EPA's concurrence on an exceptional events request submitted by the Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE) on February 19, 2026, and concurred on by the EPA on March 24, 2026. Therefore, the EPA is taking final agency action on Michigan's exceptional events request. This action fulfills the EPA's statutory obligation to determine whether the Detroit area attained the 2015 ozone NAAQS by the Moderate attainment date of August 3, 2024.
items.title: Air Plan Approval; Michigan; Determination of Attainment by the Attainment Date for the 2015 Ozone Standards

items.summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus SAS Model A350-941 airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report of a missing main landing gear (MLG) brake rod center pin nut sub-assembly detected during an inspection. This AD requires, depending on airplane configuration, inspection of the MLG brake rod center pin nut, lock ring, and end plate, inspection of the MLG brake rod center pin and nut, and applicable corrective actions. This AD also requires additional work for certain airplanes. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

items.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Bombardier, Inc., Model CL-600-2B16 (604 Variants) airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of cracks being found on the lower wing plank at the rear spar wing station (WS) 59 to WS 65 web and/or flange. This proposed AD would require inspecting the lower wing plank rear spar web and lower flange, the forward surface of the pressure bulkhead frame under the stiffeners, and the vertical stabilizer front spar to frame attachment fitting lower legs for cracks, and repair or rectification if applicable. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF LABOR Employment and Training Administration 20 CFR Part 604 [Docket No. ETA-2026-0100] RIN 1205-AC31 Unemployment Insurance Program National Minimum Weekly Work Search Requirements AGENCY: Employment and Training Administrati
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Labor (Department), through the Employment and Training Administration (ETA), is proposing to amend 20 CFR part 604 both to reflect a 2012 update in Federal law in which Congress, by amending section 303(a) of the Social Security Act (SSA), established a Federal work search requirement; and to establish a national minimum weekly work search requirement standard for the Federal-State unemployment compensation (UC) program. This proposed rule would mandate, among other things, that States require individuals claiming UC to complete at least five qualifying work search activities or, where applicable, meet State-adopted points-based system requirements amounting to five qualifying activities or satisfy equivalent labor force attachment criteria, each week for which UC is claimed; that individuals report their work search activities as part of their certification process prior to payment being issued; and that State law allow for certain qualifying work search activities beyond simply employer contacts. This action is necessary to reduce inconsistencies beyond those created by local labor markets in State-level requirements for individuals to actively seek work. [official summary truncated; see source]
items.title: Unemployment Insurance Program National Minimum Weekly Work Search Requirements

items.summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2021-13-20, which applies to certain Airbus Canada Limited Partnership Model BD-500-1A10 and BD-500-1A11 airplanes. Since the FAA issued AD 2021-13-20, the FAA has determined that a full secondary fuel vapor barrier must be applied. This proposed AD would retain all requirements of AD 2021-13-20 and would also require, for certain airplanes, an additional inspection of the waste box, waste access doubler, and waste service door for corrosion, and applicable on-condition actions. items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-13796; Project Identifier MCAI-2026-00015-R] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; Leonardo S.p.a. Helicopters AGENCY: Federal Aviation Admin
items.summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-05-07, which applies to all Leonardo S.p.a. Model AW189 helicopters. AD 2024-05-07 requires revising the airworthiness limitations section (ALS) of the existing helicopter maintenance manual or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-05-07, it was determined that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This proposed AD would require revising the ALS of the existing maintenance manual or ICA and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Leonardo S.p.a. Helicopters

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE Food and Nutrition Administration 7 CFR Part 273 [FNA-2026-0661] RIN 0584-AF10 Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Reforming Categorical Eligibility AGENCY: Food and Nutrition Administration (FNA), USDA. ACT
items.summary: Under section 5(a) of the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, households in which each member receives benefits under a State program funded by Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) are categorically eligible for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). Current SNAP regulations consider TANF benefits to include both cash assistance and non-cash or in-kind benefits or services from TANF-funded programs. This proposal would limit categorical eligibility to only households that receive TANF assistance, as defined at 45 CFR 260.31. These revisions would ensure that SNAP benefits are targeted to needy households that have qualified for TANF assistance while still aligning categorical eligibility's statutory purpose of simplifying program administration. A 100-word summary of this rule has been posted to www.regulations.gov and can be found here.
items.title: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Reforming Categorical Eligibility

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE Food and Nutrition Administration 7 CFR Parts 271 and 273 [FNA-2025-0368] RIN 0584-AF09 Modification to Work Requirements for Able-Bodied Adults AGENCY: Food and Nutrition Administration (FNA), USDA. ACTION: Propos
items.summary: The proposed rule would codify USDA's regulatory implementation of provisions of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025 (OBBB) changing the three-month time limit for certain participants subject to work requirements in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). These changes include modifying the list of exceptions from the time limit for certain populations; updating requirements for areas to qualify for waivers of the time limit; and adding the temporary good faith exemptions in Alaska and Hawaii. Additionally, this rule proposes to strengthen requirements for requesting waivers of the time limit and revise the SNAP definition of a homeless individual.
items.title: Modification to Work Requirements for Able-Bodied Adults

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 25 [Docket No. FAA-2026-9408; Special Conditions No. 25-897-SC] Special Conditions: Gulfstream Aerospace Corporation, Model GVII-G400 Airplane; Flight Envelope Protect
items.summary: These special conditions are issued for the Gulfstream Aerospace Corporation (Gulfstream) Model GVII-G400 airplane. This airplane will have a novel or unusual design feature when compared to the state of technology envisioned in the airworthiness standards for transport category airplanes. This design feature is an envelope protection function to protect the airplane from over- and rapid-rotation on takeoff. The applicable airworthiness regulations do not contain adequate or appropriate safety standards for this design feature. These special conditions contain the additional safety standards that the Administrator considers necessary to establish a level of safety equivalent to that established by the existing airworthiness standards.
items.title: Special Conditions: Gulfstream Aerospace Corporation, Model GVII-G400 Airplane; Flight Envelope Protection: Takeoff Stall Protection

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Parts 91, 125, 135, 137, and 145 [Docket No.: FAA-2024-0025 Amdt. Nos. 91-385, 125-78, 135-150, 137-18, and 145-34] RIN 2120-AL20 Inspection Programs for Single-Engine Turb
items.summary: The final rule updates the maintenance inspection requirements for single-engine turbine-powered airplanes and unmanned aircraft. Aircraft owners and operators now have more inspection program options to choose from and more relaxed mechanical reliability reporting requirements. It also clarifies various maintenance-related regulations. This final rule relieves aircraft owners, operators, maintenance providers, and FAA of certain workload burdens by facilitating a more efficient workload for these individuals without compromising aviation safety.
items.title: Inspection Programs for Single-Engine Turbine-Powered Airplanes and Unmanned Aircraft; and Miscellaneous Maintenance-Related Updates
